item.title: Labour Angst Over Migrants and Welfare Will Test Burnham’s Backbone
item.description: If there’s one thing Andy Burnham’s friends and enemies can agree on, it’s that the UK prime minister is “a nice guy.” Niceness is a bankable political asset. The PM’s allies point to an immediate “Burnham bounce” — his approval ratings are up in every demographic, except right-wing Reform UK voters. What’s more, his upbeat style has paid dividends in a three-point increase in GfK’s consumer confidence index this month, to its highest level since Labour took power two years ago.
item.dc:creator: Martin Ivens

item.title: AfD: German Far-Right Firewall Is Facing Historic Threat in Saxony-Anhalt Vote
item.description: “Let’s write history together” is a phrase one wouldn’t ordinarily associate with regional elections, which tend to be about local concerns rather than epochal change. Yet ahead of an upcoming state vote in Germany, the slogan has become ubiquitous at rallies of the buoyant far-right Alternative für Deutschland.
item.dc:creator: Katja Hoyer

item.title: Nepal-China: To Fix Flood Disasters, We Need More Giant Dams
item.description: In the popular imagination, there’s only one threat to picturesque mountain landscapes that can compete with the destruction wrought by flood disasters like the torrent that swept through valleys on the Nepalese-Chinese border: dams.
item.dc:creator: David Fickling

item.title: Billionaire Justin Sun’s Bride Price Stunt Prolongs Crypto Winter
item.description: Just when Bitcoin seemed to be breaking out of its long winter, a publicity stunt by one of the crypto industry’s most prominent billionaires is raising questions as to whether this asset class should be in mainstream investors’ portfolios.
item.dc:creator: Shuli Ren

item.title: Hollywood Is in Trouble But Wall Street Is Undefeated
item.description: Will AI do to Los Angeles what radio did to Tin Pan Alley?
item.dc:creator: Jessica Karl

item.title: Don’t Hedge the KPIs
item.description: KPI hedging, KPI insider trading, leveraged ETF education and seized Anthropic shares.

item.title: China’s Proya Cosmetics Giant Has Its Ulta Strategy in US Backwards
item.description: With sales stalling due to relentless competition, Proya Cosmetics Co. is right to look overseas for the next growth engine. But China’s biggest beauty company is getting ahead of itself by announcing distribution at Ulta Beauty Inc. without first building meaningful name recognition among American shoppers.
item.dc:creator: Juliana Liu

item.title: The US Economy Needs Silicon Valley, Wall Street and Hollywood
item.description: Even more so than usual, Hollywood’s future is uncertain. For decades the Los Angeles economy revolved around the film industry, but now more movies and shows are filmed elsewhere, driven or lured away by high expenses or tax incentives. The prospect of Paramount leaving California over the state’s antitrust lawsuit may not be serious, but the very idea that it can be entertained shows how much the economics of the industry have changed.
item.dc:creator: Allison Schrager

item.title: Colorado River Cuts Will Force Southwest to Choose Between Cows and People
item.description: Sustaining communities of millions of thirsty people in a desert is challenging enough. Adding millions more cows, or at least growing the water-intensive food those cows eat, ramps up the difficulty level exponentially. America’s arid Southwest is learning it can’t comfortably have both.
item.dc:creator: Mark Gongloff

item.title: For the New CDC Director, Damage Control Would Be a Big Win
item.description: Through little fault of her own, the nation’s new head of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention starts her job with low expectations. It’s not just her boss’s antipathy for the agency, which he has called a “cesspool of corruption.” Within days of Erica Schwartz’s confirmation as director, the president issued an executive order seeking to overhaul the childhood vaccine schedule — with no new supporting evidence.
item.dc:creator: The Editors

item.title: Measles Outbreak Exposes Florida Republicans’ Vaccine Problem
item.description: Republicans have painted themselves into a corner by undermining vaccines. Nowhere is this clearer than Florida, where the outgoing Republican governor and his potential successor have tried to use vaccine mandates to align themselves with President Donald Trump’s politically risky position.
item.dc:creator: Mary Ellen Klas

item.title: Big Tech Cannot Be Trusted to Regulate Its AI Creations
item.description: Bill Gates, the billionaire co-founder of Microsoft Corp., published a 6,000-word essay on Aug. 26 saying that he would slow the development of artificial intelligence if he could.
